source_claims.statement: LLM ideation from RFC micro-fragments (138 RFCs → 15k fragments → 30k vectors). Broad prompts produced low novelty; micro-inspiration improved rediscovery of unpublished techniques.

Tested on 30k authorized sites. LLMs struggled with HTTP mechanics, over-anchored, produced known triggers. Weaponization required human intervention and prompt workarounds (renaming, placebo features).
Findings fed back to generate new hypotheses. Major conceptual leaps (Shared-Parser Confusion) needed human validation.

research_questions.formulation: Can an LLM-driven system, given micro-fragments of RFCs rather than broad prompts, generate and prove novel HTTP desync triggers that human researchers had not previously published?
research_questions.anchor: core research question of the paper
research_questions.uncertainty_reduced: whether AI can produce novel protocol-level findings under constrained inspiration
research_questions.assumption_challenged: that LLMs only rediscover known techniques

environment_model_updates: HTTP desync surface is large and context-dependent
Evaluation harness must separate trigger discovery from weaponization
Anomaly detection can surface non-desync issues

systematic_vs_exploratory.exploratory: cascade from findings to new hypotheses; anomaly detection

negative_inconclusive: Autonomous weaponization: high false positives, safety refusals, poor HTTP understanding
unobserved_history: exact prompt iterations that raised rediscovery from 0% to 30%
forbidden_inferences: Do not treat AI-discovered triggers as fully autonomous novel research without the human design of the harness and inspiration method
Failure of autonomous weaponization does not falsify the trigger-generation approach
next_evidence_actions: Note tool releases and Black Hat/DEF CON presentations
layer_b_candidate_principles: Micro-inspiration from primary specifications (RFC fragments) can produce higher novelty than broad prompts
Separate trigger discovery from weaponization; the latter often requires stronger human or deterministic gates
Anomaly detection on large-scale differential tests can surface unexpected issue classes
model_vs_harness: Hypothesis generation from RFC fragments is model; large-scale differential evaluation, anomaly detection, and validation gates are primarily harness.
